story.headline: Reports Indicate DeepSeek and Moonshot AI Relied on OpenAI Models for Training
story.summary: Reports indicate that Chinese AI developers DeepSeek and Moonshot AI allegedly used distillation techniques on outputs and protected reasoning from OpenAI models. The practice highlights ongoing scrutiny over how competitive AI architectures are trained using frontier model outputs.

draft.body:
Chinese artificial intelligence developers DeepSeek and Moonshot AI relied heavily on outputs from OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train their latest AI systems, according to a report published on October 28, 2026, by [The Information](https://thenextweb.com/news/deepseek-moonshot-gpt-6-astra-distillation). The reporting, cited by news outlets including [Reuters and Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/openais-astra-used-by-chinese-ai-firms-to-train-models-the-information-93CH-4981331), relies on sources with direct knowledge of the engineering efforts and sheds light on the widespread use of distillation to build competing frontier models.

The technique, known as model distillation, involves querying an advanced system at scale and using its answers and reasoning patterns as synthetic training data for another system. While distillation is common across the sector for creating smaller internal variants, American frontier labs maintain strict rules barring competitors from using their outputs to develop commercial substitutes.

## The Distillation Reports and Models Involved

According to reporting detailed by [Gadgets Now](https://gadgetsnow.indiatimes.com/tech-news/deepseek-and-moonshot-ai-reportedly-used-openai-models-to-train-their-latest-ai-systems/articleshow/135295755.cms), two specific Chinese models allegedly benefited from GPT-6 Astra outputs during their development cycles. The first is Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro, which was released the week prior to the report. The second is an updated version of DeepSeek's V4.1-Flash, designated V4.1-Flash 1017, which was released on October 17, 2026.

DeepSeek previously positioned V4.1-Flash in September as an inexpensive alternative to Western systems, while Moonshot claimed Kimi K3.1 Pro outperformed GPT-6 Astra on an internal coding benchmark. Neither developer's self-reported performance benchmarks have been independently verified. Neither Moonshot nor DeepSeek has publicly confirmed using Astra outputs, and Moonshot declined to comment while DeepSeek did not respond to press inquiries.

[[FIG1]]

## Shifting Targets After Claude Defenses Tightened

The focus on OpenAI's infrastructure comes as other frontier providers have rolled out technical barriers against systematic data extraction. As reported by [The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/openais-astra-becomes-the-main-target-for-chinese-ai-labs-after-anthropic-tightens-its-defenses/), Chinese developers previously leaned on Anthropic's Claude models, but Anthropic stated in October 2026 that new safeguards reduced the volume of data harvested during suspected distillation attacks by 90% to 99%.

Anthropic had previously disclosed that external campaigns tied to DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, and MiniMax accounted for more than 16 million interactions across roughly 24,000 fraudulent user accounts. As Anthropic tightened its perimeter, technical teams focused their extraction efforts on GPT-6 Astra to gather complex reasoning traces necessary to train comparable systems.

## OpenAI's Disrupted Extraction Campaign

While the report from The Information adds specifics regarding Kimi K3.1 Pro and V4.1-Flash, OpenAI had already publicly documented unauthorized probing earlier in the autumn. In a post published on September 30, 2026, [OpenAI detailed a coordinated campaign](https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/chinese-ai-giants-deepseek-moonshot-used-openais-gpt-6-astra-to-train-their-models-report-101793247532638.html) that began on July 1, 2026, designed to extract protected internal reasoning from its models.

OpenAI stated that the activity escalated sharply on July 24 and July 25, generating 16,000 requests from more than 4,000 user accounts. OpenAI attributed a core cluster of the activity to individuals linked to Moonshot AI, while uncovering related activity across a network of more than 15,000 users. OpenAI reported that it terminated the accounts and disrupted the campaign on July 28, confirming that internal databases and customer communications were not breached or compromised.

[[FIG2]]

## Terms of Service and Geopolitical Tensions

The reports highlight deepening technical and regulatory friction between Western frontier labs and Chinese developers. OpenAI's official Usage Policies explicitly prohibit using model outputs to train competing services that substitute for its offerings. On October 21, 2026, OpenAI published an updated usage framework that takes effect on November 20, 2026.

Beyond commercial policy violations, the practice continues to draw scrutiny from policymakers. The Trump administration previously barred civilian United States government agencies from deploying DeepSeek products due to national security concerns regarding Chinese operations. OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google have warned that distillation allows competitors to replicate capabilities without making comparable investments, while OpenAI specifically cautioned that extracting protected reasoning bypasses safety protections.

faq.a: AI distillation is a training method where developers query a capable model and use its responses as training data to improve a smaller, cheaper, or newer model without building all features from scratch.

faq.q: Which models were reportedly trained on GPT-6 Astra?
faq.a: According to reporting from The Information, the models include Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro and DeepSeek's updated V4.1-Flash 1017, both released in October 2026.

faq.q: What actions did OpenAI take regarding unauthorized distillation?
faq.a: On September 30, 2026, OpenAI revealed it had traced an adversarial extraction campaign back to individuals linked to Moonshot AI, disrupting activity across a network of more than 15,000 users and banning the accounts involved by July 28.
